common_rules.on_missing_or_invalid_evidence: fail closed, keep the task or wave blocked, and record the exact missing or invalid evidence identity

verification_levels.name: Packet focused verification
verification_levels.required_for: every Task Card attempt before review submission

command_categories.rule: Implement the approved Task Card contract first, then run the named command and require every acceptance assertion to pass. No pre-implementation failure run is required.
Use the applicable formatter for non-Rust client files and verify the actual changed set is a subset of the immutable WorkPacket write paths.

command_categories.required_when: task.task_type == contract or candidate_write_paths include docs/schemas
command_categories.rule: Contract changes must add a negative fixture and prove old or malformed data fails according to the versioned contract.

freshness_rules: The post-implementation focused run is executed against the exact packet commit submitted for review.
The verifier reruns the focused command in a clean worktree after the implementer commit exists.
Any packet commit, base commit, dependency commit, contract hash, or test fixture change invalidates the focused VerificationPacket.
approval_rules: A Task Card with requires_approval=true must carry an unrevoked approval bound to task_id, packet commit, and acceptance scope before integration.
Contract, auth, security, policy, schema, and release-workflow packets require their declared exclusive owner and Contract or Security Controller review.
fail_closed_rules: A missing, failed, skipped, or unrelated post-implementation focused run blocks the packet until the implementation or verification contract is corrected.
A changed path outside the immutable WorkPacket scope produces scope_violation and quarantines the attempt.
A timeout, crash, skipped test, ignored test, malformed evidence, or unverified acceptance assertion is a failed gate.

verification_levels.name: Domain contract and behavior verification
verification_levels.required_for: every domain staging branch before its accepted commits can enter a global integration train

command_categories.command_source: all accepted Task Card verification commands for the domain staging commit
command_categories.rule: Run the complete crate, integration-test, or client-test surface affected by the domain, not only the last packet filter.
Run the domain exit task after all of its dependencies are accepted in the same domain staging baseline.
Run when the domain consumes or produces a public runtime, tool, workflow, app-server, plugin, client, or evidence contract.
Exercise the domain-specific malformed input, denied permission, timeout, cancellation, restart, corruption, stale-state, and unavailable-backend cases that apply.

freshness_rules: Domain verification runs after the latest accepted packet commit is present in the domain staging commit.
A new domain packet, dependency commit, public contract hash, schema fixture, or ownership boundary invalidates the prior domain evidence.
The domain exit command and capability coverage are regenerated for the exact domain staging commit proposed for integration.
approval_rules: The Domain Lead and an independent Fresh Verifier must accept the same staging commit.
Any task-level required approval remains required and cannot be replaced by Domain Lead approval.
A public contract change requires the matching exclusive ownership package and Contract Controller approval.
fail_closed_rules: Any applicable capability below behavior_verified blocks Domain Done unless an explicit Product Owner exclusion approval exists.
Any open P0 or P1, flaky required test, unowned path, stale contract hash, or unexplained scope deviation blocks the domain.
A schema-only, API-only, test-name-only, or documentation-only artifact cannot satisfy behavior verification.

verification_levels.name: Stress and repository integration verification
verification_levels.required_for: every merge train and every W3 through W5 wave exit

command_categories.rule: Run applicable concurrency, crash-window, restart, retry, and recovery tests with fixed seeds at least three times in serial and default-parallel modes.

command_categories.execution_rule: The command must run under the accepted D18-01 bounded watchdog and capture the last active test and process wait state on timeout.
Local release evidence proves repository-local behavior only and cannot satisfy external commercial proof.

command_categories.required_when: the train changes P26 client paths or contains D12 tasks

freshness_rules: Every command runs on the exact candidate integration commit in a clean worktree after the train is assembled.
Any train membership, candidate commit, Cargo.lock, client lockfile, schema, workflow, toolchain, target, or dependency change invalidates the integration packet.
Repository verification must complete before the canonical fast-forward and must be repeated after any rebase or conflict resolution.
approval_rules: The Global Merge Controller and a Fresh Verifier must approve the exact candidate commit.
Auth, security, policy, schema, Cargo.lock, release workflow, migration, and cross-platform sandbox changes run in a single-packet train with the responsible controller approval.
Canonical integration is a fast-forward performed by the single Global Merge Controller only.
fail_closed_rules: A hang, watchdog termination, test flake after three fixed-seed repeats, workspace failure, schema failure, or local-RC failure rejects the train.
A passing serial run cannot replace a failing default-parallel run, and a passing rerun cannot erase the original unexplained failure.
A stale base, fencing mismatch, path conflict, semantic lock conflict, or verification backlog over two micro-waves stops new integration dispatch.

verification_levels.name: Platform and commercial release verification
verification_levels.required_for: W6 exit, stable channel promotion, and Program Done

command_categories.rule: Build and verify Linux, macOS, and Windows artifacts on native clean release runners.
Verify offline operation, signed entitlement enforcement, expiry, revocation, issuer, customer, product, and clock rollback behavior.
Exercise real provider text and tools, remote round trip, MCP transport, and Web or IDE client against the release candidate.
Verify trusted signatures, notarization, checksums, channel manifests, rollback pointer, customer acceptance, and zero strict blockers.

freshness_rules: Every proof binds the same immutable release-candidate source commit and artifact manifest digest.
Platform, signature, notarization, offline, and channel evidence is generated after the candidate artifact digest and before stable promotion.
Live provider, remote, MCP, and client evidence is generated no more than 86400 seconds before the D18-10 blocker report.
Entitlement and signing evidence is valid at blocker-report time and is invalid immediately after expiry, revocation, issuer removal, trust-root change, or artifact hash change.
Customer acceptance remains valid only for the named version and artifact digest and is invalidated by release-candidate replacement.
approval_rules: D18-03 through D18-10 require approvals bound to their exact task, release candidate, artifact hashes, and evidence hashes.
The Release Controller approves promotion, Release Security approves signing, notarization, provenance, and platform security, and the named Customer Acceptance Owner approves product acceptance.
A Product Owner must approve every excluded reference capability before Program Done.
No implementer, release script, repository-local fixture, or model-generated text can approve its own commercial proof.
fail_closed_rules: Missing credentials, mock endpoints, fake providers, local-only MCP, schema-only clients, skipped cells, or local-RC reports cannot satisfy live commercial evidence.
Self-signed, example, expired, revoked, untrusted-issuer, wrong-customer, wrong-product, wrong-version, or hash-mismatched proof is rejected.
Any missing platform, signature, notarization, entitlement, channel, support, operations, or customer acceptance proof restores its blocker and stops promotion.
D18-10 must exit zero and report local_blocking=0, external_blocking=0, and blocking=0 without skip or bypass flags.
